# `Browser.Permission`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Permission — query and watch browser permission state via
`navigator.permissions.query({ name })` from Ipê browser apps, over
`Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: an outbound `JsCmd` requests a state snapshot (`query`) or begins
a continuous change stream (`watch`), and an inbound `JsMsg` carries the typed
`PermissionState` reply or a typed denial. Both cross the same seal codec and
fail-closed port discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses `js-port:permission`
(import-derived, keyed on the canonical `Ipe.Browser.Permission` path prefix via
`WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the top-level app's
`[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Permission.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs
    and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` wiring. The `PermissionName` type there enumerates
    all Baseline-supported permission names.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `query` returns a `Task Error PermissionState`
    via the correlated port→Task bridge; `watch` is `Cmd`-shaped, and `changes` is
    the inbound subscription folding the narrow `JsMsg` into a typed
    `Result Error PermissionState`. The inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: an
    unavailability becomes a typed `Err`, never a silently dropped variant.

## `PermissionState`

The three states the browser reports for any queried permission.

Re-exported from this module so callers import only `Ipe.Browser.Permission`.

  * `Granted` — the user (or automatic policy) has granted the permission; the
    guarded API can be called without a user gesture.
  * `Denied` — the user has explicitly denied or the site is blocked; the guarded
    API will refuse without a fresh gesture.
  * `Prompt` — no prior decision; the browser will ask the user when the guarded
    API is first called.

## `PermissionName`

Re-export of `Internals.PermissionName` — the closed set of W3C Permissions
API names (Camera, Microphone, Geolocation, Notifications, PersistentStorage,
ClipboardRead, ClipboardWrite, MidiSysex).

## `query`

```ipe
query : Internals.PermissionName -> Task Error PermissionState
```

`query name` — read the current state of a single browser permission ONCE,
as a `Task Error PermissionState`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served JS handler
(SRI-pinned, the stdlib's, never a dependency's) reaches
`navigator.permissions.query({ name })`; the typed state or a typed
unavailability resolves the `Task` directly, with no companion subscription
needed.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:permission`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort Permission ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `watch`

```ipe
watch : Internals.PermissionName -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`watch name` — begin a CONTINUOUS state-change stream for a single
permission; each `PermissionStatus.onchange` event delivers a fresh state on
the `changes` subscription. Outbound `Cmd`.

## `changes`

```ipe
changes : Internals.PermissionName -> (Result Error PermissionState -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`changes name toMsg` — the inbound subscription for state changes on `name`,
wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error PermissionState` — a typed state becomes `Ok`, an unavailability
a typed `Err`.
